design / ai-planning · delta

The plan, drawn as it is written

MOTIR-6294 · story MOTIR-6158. A DELTA mock: the planning surface's left pane while a plan is generating — for Motir AI and for an agent writing over MCP alike — and the moment it stops.

It COMPOSES, and does not redraw: PlanProposalViews (Part XXI), its PlanReviewCanvas and PlanProposalList (Parts VIII, IX, XIII), Part VI's op treatments, the canvas's edge variants and off-level anchor, ProjectRoadmapCanvas's breadcrumb and MOTIR-6161's follow offer, PlanChangeConfirmBar (Part XXII) and PlanChangeRail. Every one of them is the shipped markup, rendered from the real component on origin/main @ 34b43b9ff.

Read it as an interaction spec. Each motion is a row of numbered frames; a "during" frame is the real render with the moving element held at its mid-transition value. Durations, easings and the reduced-motion forms are in design-notes.md Part XXIII §23.3–23.5. The fixture plan is this story's own level: two committed children of MOTIR-6158 (one done, one in progress) and the proposals arriving around them.

Sheet 1 — the pane while the plan is being WRITTEN: four statesWhile a plan is generating the left pane is the same PlanProposalViews Part XXI mounts for a proposed plan, fed by a live read. What differs is small and all of it is here: no bar in the footer slot, a quiet live marker at the right end of the pane header, and the arrivals count in the breadcrumb row.

After three failed reads in a row the header’s marker says so, quietly: a warning dot and Reconnecting — showing the last update. The last good snapshot stays drawn; nothing is cleared, dimmed or alerted. The next good read restores Being written.
Sheet 2 — a card ARRIVES: the level makes room, the card enters, then its arrowsA lay batch carrying The generating pane goes live, blocked_by the two cards already drawn. Adding it re-lays the level (dependency rank decides the columns), so it is STAGED, never simultaneous: ② the cards already drawn GLIDE to their new cells, their arrows hidden for the glide · ③ the new card ENTERS the cell that is now free (fade + a 6px rise) · ④ every arrow the batch touched fades in on its final route, the new card’s two among them · ⑤ settled — exactly what the review draws for these three cards. Several cards in one batch enter together, staggered.

Sheet 6 — a DEEPEN: the card changes in place, and says so onceThe author phase fills in a body, a type, a title (update_plan_item). Sheet 7 — the OFF-LEVEL count, and why it never jumpsArrivals on a level the reader is not viewing are COUNTED in the breadcrumb row and never jumped to. One slot, in the shipped follow-offer’s markup: one level → N new in <key> · Go there; several → N new elsewhere · latest in <key> · Go there, which goes to the latest. MOTIR-6161’s offer wins the slot when it is up, because it already names where the plan lands.

Sheet 8 — REDUCED MOTION: every change, with nothing movingUnder prefers-reduced-motion: reduce nothing fades, rises, shrinks or glides: the level is simply redrawn in its new state. Each change still READS as one — an arrival and a deepen take the same 2px accent outline, held and then removed without a fade; an exit and a rewire are their end state; the arrivals count and the live marker are unchanged, because neither moves.

Sheet 9 — the LIST is live tooThe same pane, the other body. Rows appear in the order the plan receives them, with the card’s own entrance (fade + a 4px rise), and a withdrawn row leaves with the exit. Before anything has arrived the list says so in the present tense — the shipped empty statement (“This plan finished without proposing anything. Declining ends it…”) is false while a plan is still being written.

Sheet 10 — the RAIL: a hosted run beside an MCP session with no turnsMotir AI’s conversation is on the rail, and its hand-off already says the plan is being written. An agent’s conversation happened in its own harness, so the rail of an MCP-authored session has no turns. It says where the conversation was — naming the plan’s recorded authorHarness — in the rail’s own notice idiom, and the composer stays live: asking here changes the plan like any other turn.

Sheet 11 — the HAND-OVER: when the plan stops being writtengenerating → planned: the confirm bar arrives over the canvas’s bottom edge and the live marker leaves. Nothing else changes — same component, same level, same cards, same arrows, same view. generating → declined (discarded), a plan closed holding zero proposals: no bar, and the pane says so in the plan page’s own words, in the component’s band slot.
